name: vertigo overview
title: Dizziness: first decide whether it is true vertigo; non-vestibular dizziness has organic and psychiatric causes, while peripheral vertigo is named by how long attacks last and whether hearing is affected: BPPV, Meniere's disease, vestibular neuronitis or labyrinthitis, superior canal dehiscence, and aminoglycoside toxicity; each column gives presentation, investigations and treatment, with nystagmus types and vestibular physiology below

root.title: "Dizzy": is it TRUE VERTIGO, an illusion of rotary movement?
lines: history is 80% of the workup · exam: nystagmus (named by its FAST phase) and ataxia · CT, MRI
balance: vestibular + vision + position sense → brainstem, cerebellum → eye and limb muscles
one ear fails → imbalance read as rotation: eye muscles = NYSTAGMUS · higher centres = VERTIGO · limbs = ataxia · vagal nucleus = nausea, vomiting
anxiety: often the cause OR the effect · vestibular schwannoma: one-sided hearing loss + tinnitus, rarely vertigo

groups.title: YES: vestibular
lines: episodic, limited duration · hearing symptoms · nausea, vomiting, sweating, bowels · worse with head movement

tiers.title: How long does an attack last, and is hearing lost?
lines: seconds: BPPV, dehiscence · minutes to hours: Ménière's (hearing lost) or migrainous (hearing kept) · days: labyrinthitis (hearing lost) or neuronitis (kept) · forever: uncompensated vestibular loss

head: h
Not vestibular
inv: cardiac or neurological symptoms, loss of consciousness

head: h
BPPV
benign paroxysmal positional vertigo · commonest end-organ disorder
pres: • set off by specific head movements
• otoconia loose from the utricle float in the POSTERIOR canal (canalithiasis)
• idiopathic (degenerative) or head trauma (commonest cause of bilateral)
inv: • brief, fades, reverses on sitting up

head: h
Superior canal dehiscence
a third mobile window into the inner ear
pres: Vertigo with LOUD SOUND or PRESSURE
• hears own voice (autophony), footsteps, eye movements
• sound evokes vertical-torsional eye movements in the superior canal's plane

head: h
Ménière's disease
endolymphatic hydrops · 2nd commonest
50-100 per 100,000 · 10% of dizzy clinic visits
onset 40s, then 50s, 30s · familial < 10%
pres: exacerbations, remissions · hard to judge treatment
inv: ↓ endolymph resorption or ↑ production (stria vascularis, dark cells) · hydrops ≠ always Ménière's
tx: low salt · no caffeine, chocolate, alcohol, tobacco

head: h
Vestibular neuronitis / labyrinthitis
viral, often after a cold
pres: • nystagmus beats AWAY from the bad ear

head: h
Aminoglycoside toxicity
ear drops or injections
pres: vertigo, nystagmus beating away from it

panels.title: Nystagmus
items: slow phase = vestibulo-ocular reflex · fast phase = saccade that resets the eye
caloric COWS: Cold → fast phase Opposite, Warm → Same · tests the brainstem in coma (needs the MLF for conjugate eyes)
peripheral (spontaneous vestibular): direction FIXED, mostly horizontal, SUPPRESSED by fixation
other pathologic: positional · gaze-paretic · rebound · fixation · congenital · dissociated

panels.title: Vestibular physiology
items: hair cells (CN VIII): bending toward the kinocilium opens K+ channels → depolarizes
resting firing ~100/s, so each afferent signals BOTH directions
otoliths (utricle, saccule): linear movement, tilt vs gravity · posture
canals: rotation · endolymph lags, pushes the cupula · gaze stabilization
canals work in PAIRS: the brain reads the difference, so one dead ear = false rotation
VOR: 3 neurons, eyes compensate in 10-15 ms
